prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset: five Minecraft magical thread sprites, actual native pixel-grid design.

Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: a nearest-neighbor enlargement of our ACTUAL 16x16 inventory textures from the fuller previous version. Each visible large square is one real item pixel. Image 2 is native Minecraft String enlarged as a shading reference.

The latest revision became much too thin and lost its shadow edge during reduction. This edit must be between the fuller target and bare one-pixel strands: slender but readable cords, generally TWO logical pixels across, one pale strand pixel plus one modest darker edge pixel. Keep each large logical square exactly the scale of Image 1. Do not invent smaller subpixels or higher-resolution detail. Preserve the five loose string arrangements and open loops in Image 1, with a small reduction in the bulky three-pixel corners. Do not shrink the overall icons or erase complete strand sections. Keep full native item footprints inside 14x14 occupied pixels with one-pixel transparent padding on a 16x16 grid.

MOST IMPORTANT: the shaded edge must follow the WHOLE strand consistently. A pale strand with a continuous modest dark companion edge should wind around each loop, through its bends and out to the loose ends. Maintain consistent light-upper/left and dark-lower/right shading, naturally wrapping the turns and finishing the ends. No naked bright stretches interrupted by random dark patches. Do not alternate solid pale runs with solid dark runs to pretend there is a shadow. Do not give only one loop a shadow and leave the next loop unshaded. At corners and crossings a short broader patch is okay; avoid a heavy border around both sides of the cord or long three-pixel-wide bands.

Use simple coherent flat shades: a soft dark material-tinted grey, a pale material strand tone, a near-white highlight, optionally one gentle intermediate shade. At most four opaque shades per sprite. Darkest pixels around RGB70-85 with the material tint: visible and continuous, never solid black, harsh ink outline or noisy speckling. The light/dark pairing in the Minecraft String reference should guide the treatment.

Exactly five sprites left to right: Ensorcelled pale lavender-blue; Callous pale silver; Smoldering pale peach/cream; Laced pale sage/mint; Consecrated warm ivory. Keep their familiar loose loop and folded-string shapes, with large transparent holes and generous separation. Similar visual weight for all five, roughly 65-80 occupied native pixels rather than sparse 40-pixel outlines or dense rope. Each string is physically connected. The overall 3:1 horizontal sheet layout and empty space around the row stay like Image 1.

Treat this as pixel artwork authored directly on each 16x16 grid. It will be reduced back to those SAME logical pixels, so preserve the full two-pixel strand/shadow structure in every section. Transparent background and holes, hard opaque pixel squares, no antialiasing, fuzzy fringes, blur, gradients, glow, random particles, smoothing, text, labels, UI, wands or additional objects.
production: Actual 16x16 export, at most four shades, binary alpha, connected strands and one-pixel padding. Fuller strands and consistent companion shading checked in the exported sprites and actual Minecraft inventory. Generated sheet is reference artwork.
